sections.content: Francis Ford Coppola's The Godfather (1972) stands as perhaps the greatest achievement in American cinema, adapting Mario Puzo's novel into a sprawling epic that examines power, family, and the American Dream through the lens of organized crime. The film follows Michael Corleone's transformation from war hero to ruthless don, anchored by Marlon Brando's iconic performance as Vito Corleone and Al Pacino's career-defining portrayal of Michael. Citizen Kane (1941) may have pioneered deep focus photography, but Coppola and cinematographer Gordon Willis created their own visual language of shadows and intimate family gatherings.
